I have been working this land my whole life. My father grew cotton here, and his father before him. The soil in Quzhou knows cotton. But I am getting old, and some of my sons and daughters are in the city now. I have to think about how much work I can handle.

I will split my 6 mu like this: 3.5 mu for spring maize and 2.5 mu for cotton. Maize is easier on my body. I do not need to bend down to pick it like cotton. My family can help at harvest but they cannot always come back from the city for long.

For the maize, I will buy hybrid seed from the cooperative in town, the same kind my neighbors use. The hybrid gives much more grain than the old seeds. I will plough under last year's cotton stalks with the rotary machine I rent. I apply urea in two goes — some at planting, some when the stalks are knee-high. I will pump the well maybe three times: once to help germination, once when it tassels, once when the grain is filling. Two sprays should handle the weeds and the corn borer.

For the cotton, I will plant Bt hybrid seed again. It saves me some spraying for bollworm, though I still need to spray for aphids and whitefly — those are bad some years. I will plough the cotton field first, the way I always do. Cotton needs more water than maize and more feeding. I have been doing this 50 years, I know when the bolls are setting and the plant is thirsty. I will irrigate four times and spray five times to be safe. Cotton income is good when the price holds.

I am not going to try anything new this year. I am 70. What I know works.
